title: Custom hooks and the rules of hooks
summary: The rules of hooks and why they exist, extracting reusable stateful logic into use-functions, what custom hooks share and what they do not, and good hook design.

sections.title: The rules of hooks
sections.body:
- Call hooks only at the **top level** of a component or custom hook: not inside conditions, loops, nested functions or after an early `return`.
- Call them only from **React functions**: components and custom hooks, not plain functions or class components.

React identifies each hook by its **call order** in a render. If a condition skips a `useState` call, every later hook reads the wrong slot. The one exception is `use`, which may be called conditionally.

sections.title: Extracting a custom hook
sections.body:
A custom hook is a function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other hooks. It lets several components reuse **stateful logic**, such as subscribing to online status, debouncing a value or reading a media query, while keeping the component focused on what to render.

Each call to a custom hook gets its **own independent state**. Two components calling `useCounter()` do not share a counter; to share state, lift it up or use context.

sections.title: Designing hooks well
sections.body:
Name hooks after **what they do**, `useOnlineStatus`, `useChatRoom`, not after lifecycle (`useMount`). Return what callers need: a value, a tuple like `useState`, or an object for many values. Keep inputs reactive: the hook re-runs on every render with the latest arguments, so list them in the inner effect's dependencies.

If a function does not call any hooks, do not name it `use…`; make it a plain helper. Prefer built-in solutions where they exist, such as `useSyncExternalStore` for subscribing to an external store.

pitfalls: Calling a hook conditionally or after an early return.
Expecting two components using the same custom hook to share state.
Naming a plain helper with a `use` prefix, or a hook without one.
Leaving hook arguments out of the inner effect's dependency array.

gotchas.question: Two sibling components both call `const [n, setN] = useCounter()`. One increments. Does the other change?
gotchas.answer: No. Each call has its own state. Custom hooks share logic, not state.

gotchas.question: Which hook may be called inside an `if`?
gotchas.answer: `use`. All other hooks must run in the same order on every render.
